questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 24 cm and a height of 7 cm. What is its area?

block.label: Quick Recall
block.sub: Four options, one answer — keep it fast

questions.why: Area equals half of base times height: ½ × 24 × 7 = 84 cm². Take your time rather than rushing to multiply.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A cylinder has radius 3 cm. What is the area of one circular end?

block.label: Scrub It
block.sub: Rub out the wrong answers with your finger

questions.why: One circular end uses πr², so π × 3² ≈ 28.3 cm². A common error is using the diameter or forgetting to square the radius.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has a base of 20 cm and a height of 4 cm. Slow down and work through it step by step: what is its area?

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: A reaction happens in an open test tube and releases a gas. Has mass actually been lost?
questions.why: Mass is never truly lost — the escaping gas carries mass away into the air, so the apparent loss is matter leaving the open system, not destruction of mass.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What do we call the leftover substances remaining after a chemical reaction finishes?
questions.why: The products are the new substances formed once reactants have chemically changed during a reaction.
